scope: Read-only runtime diagnosis of exact registered-games production service on one owned harmless hidden generic Windows process; not a game, CS2 or Steam acceptance.
production_service_dependencies: Unmodified compiled registered-games.js with default production CIM scanner, executable filesystem probe, background scheduler and getter. Only the registry file points to a newly created owned Temp directory.

finding.observed: The exact exported scanner rejected with Process scan timed out at3030ms; service snapshot also returned unavailable at3018ms for a process whose exact own PID was concurrently readable through both CIM and Get-Process. Background activity remained null.
finding.impact: On this host the current global CIM query can fail to detect even an ordinary owned readable process within the existing3-second deadline. This is an actual runtime integration failure, not proof that a particular game or anti-cheat caused it.
finding.boundary: The current3s/128KiB bounds and fail-closed unknown-running result were preserved. No arbitrary process was classified by basename alone.
finding.next: Review a provider-side WQL predicate for only the registered image names, constructed inside the fixed script from strictly validated/escaped stdin data. Re-run the same owned-process acceptance under unchanged bounds before applying or claiming a fix.
not_proven: That CS2's earlier null ExecutablePath has the same cause as this ordinary-process timeout
A filtered query fix or a WinAPI fallback

isolation.own_hidden_process: System ping to127.0.0.1 only; exact Popen child handle terminated during finally cleanup

probe_harness_qualification: Initial own diagnostic used PowerShell -File and was rejected by existing Restricted execution policy; the child was cleaned. The diagnostic was corrected to inline -Command, matching the production scanner's existing invocation. No execution policy was changed.
source_changes: None. Only a scoped verification receipt was added; no application source edit, staging, commit, installation or publication.
